_comment: The artist's STILL deliveries -- wall art, and anything else that is one image
rather than a folder of frames. Run with:
python tools/den_static_import.py --manifest tools/den_statics.json
Everything it writes under assets/main_menu/environment/static/ is OUTPUT. The
delivery in src_root is never modified. Same arrangement as tools/den_items.json
and tools/fox_clips.json.
Each set names a folder of PNGs and one scale. Sizes were chosen by measuring the
delivery against what is already in the room rather than by picking a round number:
paintings_small  1/2  144px art -> 72px, which is the existing painting.png to
the pixel. These twelve were drawn at half the size of the
rest of the set, so half scale puts them exactly where the
room's one existing painting already sits.
paintings_large  1/3  ~450px art -> ~150px. Half would be ~225px against a wall
band only 245px tall -- a painting filling 95% of the wall
floor-to-ceiling. A third leaves it reading as a statement
piece at roughly twice the small ones, which is a range
rather than a mismatch.
posters          1/1  59-120px as delivered, already den-sized and sitting
naturally between the two painting tiers. Nothing to do,
and every pixel is the artist's own.
Two tiers is deliberate, not a normalisation that was skipped. The artist drew
small framed pictures and large statement pieces, and a room with both is better
than a room where everything is one size.
'mount' is carried straight into the catalog entry. All of this hangs.
'category' likewise -- see DenCatalog.CATEGORIES.

sets._note: The twelve drawn at ~144px. Picked by size rather than by name -- see max_source_width.

Punk band posters, unframed. Delivered at den size already. Their own tab rather than sharing one with the paintings: forty-five pieces behind one tab is seven pages, and framed gallery art and band posters are nothing alike to look through.
